title: Interleaved write coalescing and priority token prefetch to reduce streaming tail latency
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Motivation: streaming workloads exhibited recurring p99 first-byte and tail-token stalls when small bursts of tokens from many concurrent streams contended on I/O and the KV read path. Prior fixes addressed batching and kernel selection, but customer traces still showed OS-level write syscalls and small socket writes as a dominant contributor to per-token overhead at low token sizes. This PR introduces two complementary runtime optimizations: (1) interleaved write coalescing on the streaming transport to amortize syscall and syscall-buffer overhead across microbatches, and (2) priority token prefetch where the scheduler issues asynchronous KV read-ahead for active priority streams to keep the KV cache warm during bursts. Design: - Interleaved write coalescing: the transport layer buffers small stream fragments (<= 512 bytes) for up to a configurable coalesce_window (default 4ms) and flushes combined frames in one syscall when safe (does not change framing semantics or ordering). Coalescing is interleaved by stream priority to avoid head-of-line blocking: higher-priority streams flush earlier within the window. This minimizes syscalls while preserving low-latency for hot streams. - Priority token prefetch: a lightweight scheduler hint that marks in-flight streams as HOT if they have produced >N tokens within the last T ms. The runtime issues non-blocking KV prefetches for the next expected KV keys for HOT streams (bounded prefetch depth 2) and escalates resource allotment temporarily (CPU tokenization and kernel pinning hints). Implementation notes: - New transport component: transport/coalesce.go with a small state machine that tracks per-socket coalesce queues and priorities. - Scheduler changes: runtime/scheduler_prefetch.go (integrates with existing batch planner), and kv/prefetch.go for read-ahead logic. - Kernel hinting: expose soft pin hints to the kernel selector for short windows during HOT status. - Configs: coalesce_window_ms, coalesce_max_bytes, hot_threshold_tokens, prefetch_depth, all exposed in runtime config with safe defaults. Tests and safety: - End-to-end deterministic tests for framing and ordering (no change to protocol semantics). - Staging perf harness (perf-canary) experiments added to validate behavior under variable load. - Added telemetry: coalesce_flush_count, coalesce_avg_window_ms, prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_cancel_rate. Benchmarks: - Microbench harness: 1k concurrent streams sending 1-8 token bursts, baseline main branch vs this PR. Observed median first-byte latency improvement ~18% and p99 first-byte improved from 124ms to 68ms on our 8-token burst synthetic (about 45% reduction). Cost impact: negligible CPU increase (<2% system CPU) while reducing per-token syscall overhead; KV prefetch increases small KV read volume but with a prefetch hit rate ~78% in workloads with repeating context. Rollout plan: - Canary in us-west with coalesce_window_ms=4 and prefetch_depth=1 for 48 hours. - Gradual ramp to 25% traffic after verification, then 100% after 7 days. Follow-ups: - Evaluate dynamic coalesce_window based on observed queuing (auto-scale window). - Combine with adaptive kernel pacing work to further reduce p50 tail. - Add per-customer override for extremely latency-sensitive SLAs.

release_notes: Improved streaming latency for small-token bursts via transport coalescing and priority KV prefetch. Configs: coalesce_window_ms (default 4), coalesce_max_bytes (default 512), hot_threshold_tokens (default 3), prefetch_depth (default 1). Safe defaults ensure no regression for latency-sensitive streams.
